Please polish the following text to make it more eloquent and professional, keeping all original information unchanged:

We formulate a quantum generalization of the notion of the group of Riemannian isometries for a compact Riemannian manifold, by introducing a natural notion of smooth and isometric action by a compact quantum group on a classical or noncommutative manifold described by spectral triples, and then proving the existence of a universal object (called the quantum isometry group) in the category of compact quantum groups acting smoothly and isometrically on a given (possibly noncommutative) manifold satisfying certain regularity assumptions. In fact, we identify the quantum isometry group with the universal object in a bigger category, namely the category of `quantum families of smooth isometries', defined along the line of Woronowicz and Soltan. We also construct a spectral triple on the Hilbert space of forms on a noncommutative manifold which is equivariant with respect to a natural unitary representation of the quantum isometry group. We give explicit description of quantum isometry groups of commutative and noncommutative tori, and in this context, obtain the quantum double torus defined in \cite{hajac} as the universal quantum group of holomorphic isometries of the noncommutative torus.

outputs.L1: We formulate a quantum generalization of the group of Riemannian isometries of a compact Riemannian manifold. To this end, we introduce a natural notion of smooth, isometric action by a compact quantum group on a classical or noncommutative manifold described by a spectral triple. Under certain regularity assumptions, we then prove the existence of a universal object—called the quantum isometry group—in the category of compact quantum groups acting smoothly and isometrically on a given, possibly noncommutative, manifold. In fact, we identify the quantum isometry group as the universal object in a broader category: the category of “quantum families of smooth isometries,” defined along the lines of Woronowicz and Soltan. We also construct a spectral triple on the Hilbert space of forms over a noncommutative manifold that is equivariant with respect to a natural unitary representation of the quantum isometry group. Finally, we provide explicit descriptions of the quantum isometry groups of commutative and noncommutative tori and, in this context, recover the quantum double torus defined in \cite{hajac} as the universal quantum group of holomorphic isometries of the noncommutative torus.

We develop a quantum analogue of the Riemannian isometry group of a compact Riemannian manifold. Using spectral triples to represent both classical and noncommutative manifolds, we define what it means for a compact quantum group to act on such a space smoothly and isometrically. Under suitable regularity conditions, we then establish the existence of a universal compact quantum group with these properties, termed the quantum isometry group.

Moreover, this quantum isometry group is shown to be universal in a broader setting: the category of “quantum families of smooth isometries,” formulated in the spirit of Woronowicz and Soltan. We also build a spectral triple on the Hilbert space of differential forms over a noncommutative manifold, equivariant under a canonical unitary representation of its quantum isometry group.

Finally, we explicitly determine the quantum isometry groups associated with both ordinary and noncommutative tori. In particular, we recover the quantum double torus introduced in \cite{hajac} as the universal quantum group governing holomorphic isometries of the noncommutative torus.

The work extends the classical notion of the Riemannian isometry group to the setting of compact quantum groups. It introduces smooth and isometric actions of compact quantum groups on both classical manifolds and noncommutative manifolds represented by spectral triples. In this framework, the geometric information encoded by a spectral triple plays the role of the Riemannian structure and makes it possible to formulate quantum analogues of smoothness and metric preservation.

Under suitable regularity assumptions on the spectral triple and the corresponding quantum group actions, the work establishes the existence of a universal compact quantum group acting smoothly and isometrically on the given manifold. This universal object is called the **quantum isometry group**. Its universality means that every other admissible compact quantum group action preserving the same geometric structure factors through it.

The quantum isometry group is further characterized as the universal object in the more general category of **quantum families of smooth isometries**. This broader formulation allows isometries to be parametrized by possibly noncommutative \(C^*\)-algebras, rather than requiring them from the outset to arise from a compact quantum group. The result therefore shows that the universal quantum family of smooth isometries naturally carries the structure of a compact quantum group.

Using the natural unitary representation of the quantum isometry group on differential forms, the work also constructs an equivariant spectral triple on the Hilbert space of forms of a noncommutative manifold. This construction demonstrates that the quantum symmetry is compatible not only with the underlying algebra and metric data, but also with the associated differential and spectral structures.

Finally, the general theory is illustrated through explicit computations for both commutative and noncommutative tori. The corresponding quantum isometry groups are described concretely, revealing how classical toral symmetries extend and deform in the quantum setting. In particular, the **quantum double torus** is identified as the universal compact quantum group of holomorphic isometries of the noncommutative torus. These examples highlight the effectiveness of the framework in producing and analyzing genuinely quantum symmetry groups.

The work develops a noncommutative analogue of the classical theory of Riemannian isometry groups. In ordinary differential geometry, the isometries of a compact Riemannian manifold form a compact Lie group acting smoothly and preserving the metric. To extend this picture to noncommutative spaces, the geometry is described by a spectral triple: an algebra represented on a Hilbert space together with a Dirac-type operator encoding metric and differential information. Compact quantum groups then replace compact Lie groups as the relevant symmetry objects.

Within this framework, the work introduces suitable notions of smooth and isometric compact quantum group actions on both classical and noncommutative manifolds. An action is required to preserve the geometric structure encoded by the spectral triple, typically through compatibility with the Dirac operator or the associated Laplacian, while also satisfying appropriate smoothness and regularity conditions on the underlying dense algebra. These requirements make it possible to formulate a category of quantum symmetries that genuinely generalizes the classical category of smooth Riemannian isometries.

Under suitable regularity assumptions, this category is shown to admit a universal object. The resulting compact quantum group is called the quantum isometry group of the spectral triple. Its universal property means that every admissible compact quantum group action by smooth isometries factors uniquely through it. The construction therefore produces the largest quantum symmetry compatible with the prescribed noncommutative geometric data. When the spectral triple comes from an ordinary compact Riemannian manifold, the construction is consistent with the classical isometry group, while in genuinely noncommutative examples it can yield a strictly quantum symmetry group.

The analysis is also extended from individual compact quantum group actions to quantum families of smooth isometries. This broader formulation allows symmetries parametrized by noncommutative algebras, even before a coproduct or full quantum group structure is imposed. The universal quantum isometry group is characterized as universal in this larger setting as well: any quantum family preserving the relevant smooth and metric structures factors through the canonical action of the universal object. This strengthens the interpretation of the quantum isometry group as the intrinsic symmetry object associated with the spectral geometry.

A further part of the work studies the differential structure induced by the original spectral triple. Using differential forms and the natural extension of the symmetry action, an equivariant spectral triple is constructed on the space of forms. The resulting operator is analogous to the Hodge–de Rham operator in classical geometry, and the compact quantum group action is shown to be compatible with it. This provides a coherent extension of the symmetry from functions to the full differential calculus and demonstrates that the universal quantum group preserves not only the metric information but also the associated higher-order geometric structure.

The general theory is illustrated through explicit computations for tori and their noncommutative deformations. These examples clarify how the abstract universal construction can be reduced to concrete generators, relations, and coactions. In the case of the noncommutative torus, the work considers symmetries compatible with its natural complex structure and determines the universal compact quantum group acting by holomorphic isometries. The resulting object is identified with the quantum double torus. Thus, a previously known compact quantum group arises naturally as the full universal symmetry group of the noncommutative torus in the holomorphic isometric category.

Overall, the work establishes a systematic bridge between Riemannian symmetry, spectral geometry, and compact quantum groups. It provides precise notions of smooth quantum isometries, proves the existence and universality of the corresponding quantum isometry group under appropriate hypotheses, extends the action to differential forms through an equivariant spectral triple, and confirms the effectiveness of the theory through explicit torus examples.
outputs.L5:
### Riemannian Geometry, Woronowicz, and Sołtan

Riemannian geometry studies spaces equipped with a metric that makes it possible to define lengths, angles, geodesics, and curvature. In noncommutative geometry, the classical algebra of functions on a manifold is replaced by a noncommutative algebra, and geometric structures must be reformulated in algebraic and operator-theoretic terms.

A fundamental framework for this development was introduced by Stanisław Lech Woronowicz through his theory of compact quantum groups. A compact quantum group is described by a noncommutative \(C^*\)-algebra together with a coproduct that generalizes the multiplication law of an ordinary compact group. Woronowicz also developed differential calculi on quantum groups, providing tools for defining analogues of differential forms, vector fields, and invariant geometric structures.

Piotr M. Sołtan contributed to the study of quantum groups and quantum symmetries, particularly through the theory of quantum families of maps and actions on noncommutative spaces. This perspective is important when one seeks a quantum analogue of the symmetry group of a Riemannian manifold. In classical geometry, isometries preserve the Riemannian metric or, equivalently under suitable conditions, commute with the Laplace operator. In the quantum setting, these requirements can be expressed as algebraic conditions on a compact quantum group action.

The interaction between Riemannian ideas, Woronowicz’s compact quantum groups, and Sołtan’s work on quantum transformations illustrates a central theme of noncommutative geometry: geometric spaces may possess symmetries that are themselves genuinely quantum. Such structures extend classical isometry groups and provide new ways to investigate finite spaces, spectral triples, quantum homogeneous spaces, and noncommutative manifolds.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write an abstract for a research paper introducing quantum isometry groups for compact classical and noncommutative manifolds using spectral triples.
counterfactuals.output: We introduce a framework for defining and studying quantum isometry groups of compact classical and noncommutative manifolds described by spectral triples. Given a compact-type spectral triple \((\mathcal A,\mathcal H,D)\), we consider compact quantum groups acting on \(\mathcal A\) by orientation-preserving isometries, implemented on \(\mathcal H\) and compatible with the Dirac operator \(D\). Under natural regularity and finite-multiplicity assumptions, we prove the existence of a universal object in the resulting category of quantum group actions and identify it as the quantum isometry group of the spectral triple. For spectral triples arising from compact Riemannian manifolds, the construction recovers the classical isometry group under appropriate commutativity conditions, while also allowing genuinely noncommutative symmetries in broader settings. We describe equivalent formulations in terms of the Laplacian and invariant functionals, establish basic structural and functorial properties, and illustrate the theory through representative examples. This approach provides a unified operator-algebraic notion of metric symmetry applicable to both classical geometry and noncommutative spaces.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

counterfactuals.prompt: Summarize a mathematical article that defines smooth isometric actions of compact quantum groups, proves the existence of a universal quantum isometry group, and computes examples for commutative and noncommutative tori.
counterfactuals.output:
The article develops a framework for **quantum symmetries of Riemannian and noncommutative spaces**.

- A smooth action of a compact quantum group is called **isometric** when it preserves the geometric operator defining the metric—typically the Laplacian on a compact Riemannian manifold, or equivalently the relevant Dirac/Laplacian data of a spectral triple. In functional-analytic terms, the induced unitary representation must commute with this operator and preserve the natural smooth subalgebra.

- The main theorem constructs a category of compact quantum groups acting smoothly and isometrically on the space and proves that, under standard compactness and discreteness assumptions on the spectral data, this category has a **universal object**. This object, denoted the quantum isometry group, acts isometrically and admits a unique quantum-group morphism onto every other admissible symmetry. The construction uses the finite-dimensional eigenspaces of the Laplacian: the universal action is assembled from universal unitary transformations of these eigenspaces, subject to relations imposed by multiplication, involution, and the geometric structure.

- For ordinary commutative tori with their flat metrics, the calculation recovers the expected classical isometry symmetries—translations together with the finite lattice symmetries preserving the metric. Thus the universal compact quantum group is commutative in the classical case.

- For noncommutative tori, the same spectral geometry leads to genuinely quantum symmetry groups. Their generators and relations are obtained from the action on Fourier modes. The resulting quantum isometry groups can be described as suitable deformations of the classical torus isometry groups; in the two-dimensional case, explicit components involve rotation-algebra-type factors. As the deformation parameter tends to zero, these quantum groups reduce to the classical isometry group of the ordinary torus.

Overall, the article shows that the classical notion of an isometry group extends naturally to noncommutative geometry: a universal symmetry object still exists, agrees with the usual group in classical examples, and becomes genuinely noncommutative for deformed spaces such as noncommutative tori.
counterfactuals.label: cf_2

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a concise academic abstract about extending Riemannian isometry groups to noncommutative geometry, including quantum families of smooth isometries and equivariant spectral triples on differential forms.
counterfactuals.output: We develop a noncommutative extension of Riemannian isometry groups using compact quantum groups acting as quantum families of smooth isometries. For a compact Riemannian manifold—or, more generally, a spectral triple—we characterize actions that preserve the smooth structure, Laplace operator, and Riemannian data. We then lift these actions to the graded algebra of differential forms and construct equivariant Hodge–de Rham spectral triples, with Dirac operator \(D=d+d^{*}\). This framework relates quantum isometry groups defined through spectral invariance to geometric symmetry on forms, clarifies the roles of orientation and volume preservation, and provides a unified setting for studying classical and genuinely noncommutative isometries.

counterfactuals.prompt: Explain the main results of a paper on universal compact quantum groups acting isometrically on spectral triples, mentioning Woronowicz–Soltan quantum families and the quantum double torus.
counterfactuals.output:
The paper develops a general construction of the **quantum isometry group of a spectral triple** \((\mathcal A,\mathcal H,D)\).

- An isometric quantum action is encoded by a unitary corepresentation \(U\) on \(\mathcal H\) whose slices commute with \(D\), while the adjoint action
  \[
  a\longmapsto U(a\otimes 1)U^*
  \]
  preserves the algebra represented by \(\mathcal A\), together with any imposed orientation or volume condition.

- Using the **Woronowicz–Sołtan notion of a quantum family of maps**, the authors first allow the parameter algebra to be an arbitrary unital \(C^*\)-algebra, rather than assuming from the outset that it is a compact quantum group. Because \(D\) has finite-dimensional eigenspaces, such a family is described by unitary matrices on those eigenspaces.

- They construct a universal parameter algebra from free universal unitary quantum groups, quotienting by the relations required to preserve the spectral-triple structure. Universality then forces a coproduct:
  \[
  \Delta(u_{ij})=\sum_k u_{ik}\otimes u_{kj}.
  \]
  The relevant coefficient algebra satisfies Woronowicz’s compact quantum-group axioms. Thus, under the paper’s standard compactness and regularity hypotheses, the category of orientation-preserving isometric actions has an initial object, denoted typically by
  \[
  \widetilde{\mathrm{QISO}}^{+}(\mathcal A,\mathcal H,D)
  \quad\text{or}\quad
  \mathrm{QISO}^{+}(\mathcal A,\mathcal H,D).
  \]
  A distinction is sometimes made between the universal group acting on the Hilbert space and its largest Woronowicz subalgebra whose adjoint action is a genuine \(C^*\)-action on \(\mathcal A\).

A central example is a spectral triple related to the torus/noncommutative torus. Its universal quantum isometry group is identified with the **quantum double torus**. This object has two torus-like sectors, analogous to the two components of a classical semidirect product \(\mathbb T^2\rtimes\mathbb Z_2\), but its algebra and coproduct mix the sectors in a genuinely quantum way; one sector can be described by a noncommutative torus algebra. Hence it is not simply the algebra of functions on an ordinary compact group.

The main significance is therefore twofold: the paper proves that quantum isometry groups exist as universal compact quantum groups for a broad class of spectral triples, and the quantum double torus example shows that even natural torus-type geometries can possess genuinely nonclassical universal symmetries.

counterfactuals.prompt: Produce a publication-style abstract for a paper proving the existence of quantum isometry groups under regularity assumptions and identifying the quantum double torus as the universal quantum group of holomorphic isometries of the noncommutative torus.
counterfactuals.output: We establish the existence of universal quantum isometry groups for a broad class of compact noncommutative manifolds satisfying natural regularity and finite-dimensionality assumptions. Starting from a regular spectral triple, we consider compact quantum group actions that preserve the associated geometric structure—equivalently, the Dirac operator or the induced Laplacian on a canonical dense subalgebra—and prove that the corresponding category admits a universal object. We then apply this framework to the noncommutative two-torus equipped with its standard complex structure. By determining the relations imposed by holomorphicity, metric preservation, and the torus commutation law, we show that the universal compact quantum group acting by holomorphic isometries is the quantum double torus. This provides an intrinsic geometric characterization of the quantum double torus and illustrates how genuinely nonclassical symmetry groups arise naturally in noncommutative complex geometry.
